chunks: And from him, from Abu Abdillah al-Barqi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Musa ibn Bakr al-Wasiti, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who borrows money and performs Hajj. He said: 'If behind him (i.e., in his possession/assets) there is something that, if an event occurs to him, would be paid off on his behalf, then there is no objection (to his Hajj being valid).'
ai.seo_question: Is a person's Hajj valid if they have outstanding debt?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that borrowing for Hajj is permissible provided the debtor has sufficient assets to settle the debt in case of death or incapacity, ensuring the creditor's right is protected. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on fulfilling financial obligations (huquq al-nas) as a prerequisite for the validity of acts of worship, distinguishing between mere ability to pay and the security of the debt against unforeseen events.
